tasks.task: Establish site setup, security, and occupant interface controls
tasks.scope: Site induction, occupied-building access protocol, exclusion zones below scaffold, emergency contact and assembly points, welfare facilities, site signage.
hazards: Occupants or unauthorised persons entering exclusion zones or active work areas
Inadequate emergency assembly point — confusion or delay in evacuation
Tripping or slip hazard from site infrastructure in occupied building corridors
Induction failure leading to occupant non-compliance with site rules
tasks.dominant_hazard: Occupants entering active drop zones — struck by falling debris or scaffold component
controls: Barricade all exclusion zones below scaffold with rigid barriers (min 1.2 m high) and 'No Entry' signage every 2 m before any work starts.

Conduct site induction for all workers covering: exclusion zone boundaries, no-go areas during active work, emergency assembly point location, scaffold handover certificate requirements, and occupant reporting line.
Brief all occupants before work commences: exclusion zones, noise/dust timing windows, emergency contact phone, assembly point location, and prohibition on entering active work areas.
Establish 24-hour occupant contact line (phone number and staffed hours) posted at building entrance and on all site notice boards.
Position security patrol or site monitor at each exclusion zone entry during active work hours to prevent unauthorised access.

Install site notice boards at main building entrance, lift lobbies, and occupant circulation zones showing: active work area map, exclusion zones, noise hours, emergency assembly point with photo, emergency contact details.
Create and display illustrated 'Site Rules' poster (A3 min) in occupied common areas: no entry to active zones, no climbing on scaffold, report debris to site contact.
Establish temporary welfare facilities (toilet, wash station, toolbox storage) outside occupied building circulation routes; sign and barricade.
Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start any elevated work until: scaffold erection permit and handover certificate are signed by licenced scaffolder, scaffold physically inspected by site supervisor, and all exclusion zones are barricaded with signage installed

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow occupant access to common areas until: site induction completed, notice boards installed, occupant briefing delivered (recorded), and floor-level hazards cleared or barricaded
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start work until: written notification delivered to all affected occupants and body corporate/strata manager
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: unauthorised person or occupant is observed in exclusion zone or active work area — immediately barricade breach point and re-brief occupants
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold handover certificate is not available or illegible, or licenced scaffolder sign-off cannot be confirmed
🛑 STOP WORK if: exclusion zone barricade is damaged, removed, or bypassed — do not resume until repaired and occupants re-briefed
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Provide site induction records (attendance sheet, content summary) to project manager before work starts.
Brief occupant facilities manager weekly on work progress, noise timing, and changes to exclusion zones or assembly points.
Maintain site notice boards daily — update emergency contact number, noise hours, and any changes to no-go zones.
Keep occupant complaint log on-site; escalate noise, access, or safety complaints to site supervisor same day.
Provide occupant emergency contact card (postcard size) to each occupied floor — include site contact, assembly point address, and site induction date.
Retain signed occupant briefing attendance sheet and all permit certificates (scaffold, handover, working at heights) on site for audit and WHS inspector access.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
Residents responsible for clearing personal items, furniture, potted plants, and non-common fixtures from balcony and work areas before each phase — area left/excluded if not cleared
Temporary access to neighbouring properties required — confirm access arrangements before commencing
Vegetation trimmed away from surfaces designated for painting or remedial works prior to commencement — area excluded if vegetation impedes access
On-site parking or provision of parking permits required for duration of works
Final inspection and agreed scope of works to be confirmed before commencement
ppe: High-visibility vest (AS/NZS 1906.4:2010 Day/Night) worn by all workers and security patrol in occupied building areas
Safety helmet (AS/NZS 1801) worn by all workers in active work zones

monitoring.critical_control: Security patrol or site monitor present at exclusion zone entry during all active work hours; no unauthorised occupant access observed.
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during active work hours; daily pre-start check of barricades and signage
monitoring.evidence: Daily site log entry confirming exclusion zone patrols conducted, occupant feedback recorded, barricade integrity verified

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues

tasks.task: Isolate and barricade occupied tenancy areas below active works
tasks.scope: Physical exclusion barriers, warning signs, no-access tape on all entry points to ground and first-floor tenancies. Exclude public and occupants from all drop zones.
hazards: Falling debris penetrating inadequate barriers or netting — struck-by injury to occupants
Occupants ignoring or removing barriers to access work zone
No-access signage not visible or understood by non-English-speaking occupants
Gaps or holes in exclusion netting — debris pass-through
tasks.dominant_hazard: Occupant struck by falling object — barrier failure or non-compliance
controls: Install exclusion netting to full height of facade work zone with no gaps larger than 10 mm; secure to scaffold frame and perimeter edge every 0.5 m.
Post warning signs in English and pictogram format at all entry points to affected tenancies: 'DANGER — Falling Objects — No Entry' — minimum A3 size, visible from 3 metres.
Apply red and white hazard tape across all entry doors to ground and first-floor tenancies; tape must be replaced when removed or damaged.
Brief occupants in writing (translated if language identified on intake) of work schedule, exclusion zone boundaries, and access restrictions before work commences.
Assign site contact (name and mobile) to occupants for barrier breach reports or debris incidents; display contact number at all access points.
Conduct daily visual check of all barriers, netting, and signage; repair or replace any damaged section within 2 hours or stop work in affected area.
Prohibit storage of materials, waste, or equipment on ledges, windowsills, or exposed surfaces above excluded tenancies.
Remove or lock out waste chutes and downpipes in exclusion zone; do not use as debris disposal during active works below.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start active facade works until: exclusion netting is fully installed, inspected for gaps, signed off by Site Supervisor, and occupants have received written briefing of work schedule and exclusion boundaries.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: exclusion netting is breached, torn, or has gaps larger than 10 mm and cannot be repaired within 2 hours.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupants are observed inside exclusion zone or barriers have been removed without Site Supervisor approval.
🛑 STOP WORK if: warning signage is not visible, has been removed, or non-English-speaking occupants report they do not understand access restrictions.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain confirmed list of occupied tenancies, occupant contact details, and access patterns from building manager before isolation work starts.
Translate warning signage and occupant briefing into languages identified on site intake or confirmed by building manager.
Record daily barrier inspection in site log; note repairs, replacements, and any occupant non-compliance incidents.
Provide occupants with emergency contact (Site Supervisor name and mobile) in writing and posted at all affected entry points.
Brief all workers on prohibition of dropping materials, waste, or tools into exclusion zone; no exceptions for 'controlled' drops.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: High-visibility shirt or vest (AS/NZS 1906.4:2010 Day/Twilight or Day only as site risk assessment confirms)
Hard hat (AS/NZS 1801:2015) when installing, repairing, or accessing netting or barriers above head height

monitoring.critical_control: Daily visual check of exclusion netting for holes, tears, gaps >10 mm, tape intact, signage visible and legible.
monitoring.who: Site Supervisor and barrier installer each shift start and before active works above exclusion zone.
monitoring.frequency: Before each work shift and continuous visual during active works above occupied tenancies.
monitoring.evidence: Site log entry with date, time, condition of netting, signage, tape, any repairs/replacements completed, occupant contact attempts, and supervisor name/initials.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Isolate and barricade occupied tenancy
responsibility.WKR: Perform Isolate and barricade occupied tenancy per SWMS

tasks.task: Remove existing render and failed finish coatings by abrasive blast or scraping
tasks.scope: Strip acrylic render and coating from all facade panels. Contain silica dust (wet abrasive or vacuum-help method). Manage waste separation. Do not create airborne silica in occupied areas.
hazards: Respirable silica dust inhalation — abrasive blasting creates airborne silica in or near occupied areas
Uncontrolled dust migration into occupied tenancies or common areas
Inadequate respiratory protection if wet method or vacuum-help fails
Work-at-height hazard during scraping or blast nozzle control on elevated facade
Noise exposure during abrasive blasting — hearing damage without protection
tasks.dominant_hazard: Respirable silica inhalation — acute or cumulative lung disease (silicosis risk)
controls: Use wet abrasive blasting or vacuum-help extraction method — no dry blasting or scraping without dust suppression on facade above ground level.
Establish exclusion zone minimum 5m radius around blast work area — barricade, signage, no entry to occupied tenancies below active work.
Operate dust extraction plant or wet suppression system continuously during all blasting — stop work immediately if system fails or dust escapes containment.
Wear organic vapour and dust respirator (AS1716 P2 or equivalent) fitted and tested before work starts — fit test record on site.
Erect temporary polythene or containment shroud around blast zone to capture airborne dust — keep sealed and remove only when dust has settled.
Segregate waste into silica-contaminated skip — label, manage as hazardous waste stream per site waste plan.
Brief all workers and occupants below work zone on dust control method, exclusion zone limits, and stop-work triggers before blasting starts.
Monitor ambient air for dust plume escape — if visible dust migration to occupied areas occurs, stop blasting immediately and reassess method.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start abrasive blasting until: wet suppression or vacuum-help system is installed, tested, and operational; dust containment shroud is erected and sealed; exclusion zone is established and signage in place; all workers fitted with respiratory protection and fit-tested; occupant notification completed; supervisor has conducted method safety briefing.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wet suppression system fails, nozzle control is lost, or dust escapes containment zone into occupied areas below.
🛑 STOP WORK if: respiratory protection fails, comes loose, or worker reports breathing difficulty or dust ingestion.
🛑 STOP WORK if: wind speed exceeds 8 m/s or weather conditions prevent effective dust suppression (rain, low visibility).
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain signed handover certificate from licenced scaffolder before any worker uses scaffold for access.
Verify current White Card (CPCCWHS1001) and Working at Heights competency (RIIOHS204E or equivalent) for all workers at elevation.
Obtain working-at-heights permit signed before each day's elevated blasting work commences.
Obtain and display noise management plan on site — if abrasive blasting noise exceeds 85 dB(A), implement hearing protection protocol and occupant notification.
Obtain SDS for abrasive blast medium on point of use — confirm no asbestos-containing media is used.
Record fit-test date and respirator model for each worker in project WHS file.
tell building occupants minimum 24 hours before blasting — provide contact number for dust complaints during work window.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Organic vapour and dust respirator (AS1716 P2 or equivalent) — fitted and fit-tested before each use shift.
Hard hat (if working at height on scaffold).
Hearing protection (earmuffs or earplugs to AS1269) if blasting noise exceeds 85 dB(A).

monitoring.critical_control: Verify wet suppression or dust extraction system operational and dust plume contained before each shift and after any system restart.
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during active blasting; check system function each shift start and after any stoppage.
monitoring.evidence: System run-test log on site; visual confirmation of dust suppression; respirator fit-test records; occupant complaint log (nil expected).

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold and fall arrest systems, enforce exclusion zone, check SDS
responsibility.WKR: Use harness and lanyard, wear respiratory protection, report faults

tasks.task: Expose, map, and prepare concrete substrate for repair assessment
tasks.scope: Remove render from cracks and spalling zones. Map crack locations and depths on all panels. Expose reinforcement where present. Prepare surface for consultant inspection hold point.
hazards: Manual scraping or cutting creates secondary silica or dust hazard in exposed areas
Fall from height — worker on working platform with hand tools, no fall arrest engaged
Dust inhalation during exposure of cracks and spalling zones
Repetitive strain injury — prolonged scraping or chipping action
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from working platform >4m during crack exposure and mapping
controls: Install and erect scaffold to engineer design before any worker accesses platform. Verify base plates sit level on solid ground and secure all vertical and diagonal bracing per design detail.
Obtain and verify scaffold handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder. Do not allow any worker on platform until certificate is posted on site.

Wear full-body harness clipped to certified anchor point on scaffold frame during all exposure and mapping work at height. Anchor point load rating must be ≥15 kN and positioned above shoulder height.
Establish exclusion zone below working platform. Barricade with tape and signage. Restrict entry to authorised personnel only.
Wet-suppress all crack exposure and scraping work using handheld spray bottle or damp cloth. Do not dry-scrape concrete or use angle grinder dry in occupied building.
Supply SDS for any chemical admixtures, epoxy coatings, or adhesives on point of use. Brief all workers on ventilation requirements and skin contact precautions before work starts.
Provide adequate natural or mechanical ventilation in occupied spaces. Close windows and doors where practical to contain dust migration to other areas.
Limit continuous scraping or chipping to 20 minutes per worker, then rotate tasks or take 10-minute break to reduce repetitive strain injury risk.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start exposure or mapping work until: Scaffold handover certificate is signed and posted, harness anchor point is certified, and exclusion zone below platform is established and guarded.

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow consultant inspection until: All cracks mapped with depth recorded, all reinforcement exposed where visible, surface prepared (loose render removed, dust cleaned), and all mapped zones are photographed and labelled.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: Harness is detached or anchor point is damaged; scaffold shows movement, loose connections, or base plate movement; or wind speed exceeds 35 km/h.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Wet suppression fails, dust is visible migrating beyond exclusion zone, or worker becomes unwell with respiratory symptoms.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Unexpected material is exposed (suspect asbestos-cement board, hazardous coating, or structural defect) or reinforcement condition differs materially from assessment assumptions.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Verify Working at Heights Permit is signed and current before first worker accesses scaffold.
Confirm Scaffold Erection Permit is held and signed by licenced scaffolder.
Confirm all workers hold current White Card (CPCCWHS1001) and Working at Heights competency (RIIOHS204E or current RII Training Package equivalent).
Confirm scaffolder holds appropriate Scaffolding Licence for scaffold class and height.
Brief all workers on occupied building protocols: noise limits, dust containment, occupant access restrictions, and emergency assembly point.
Record crack mapping data (location, depth, size, photo reference) in site logbook before proceeding to consultant inspection hold point.
Conduct daily pre-start inspection of scaffold for damage, loose connections, base plate settlement, or unauthorised modification.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Full-body harness with certified lanyard (minimum 15 kN rated)
Hard hat (mandatory in occupied building common areas)
P2 dust mask (minimum; change if damp or blocked)
Organic vapour respirator if epoxy, solvent, or chemical admixtures are present (per SDS Section 8)

monitoring.critical_control: Harness worn and clipped to anchor point before each task; anchor point load rating certified; scaffold base and bracing intact.
monitoring.who: Supervisor (pre-start each shift); Workers (continuous during work)
monitoring.frequency: Before each worker accesses platform; continuous visual check during work; daily scaffold inspection
monitoring.evidence: Harness visual inspection tag; scaffold handover certificate posted; pre-start checklist signed; incident-free log; photographic record of mapped cracks

responsibility.SUP: Supervise repairs, check scaffold safety, approve debris controls, sign hold points
responsibility.WKR: Perform repairs per SWMS, wear PPE, use dust control, report defects

tasks.task: Hold point: Consultant inspection and repair scope approval
tasks.scope: Engage structural or façade consultant to check and approve crack stitching locations, spalling repair depths, and remedial coating strategy. Document approval before proceeding. No work on facade proceeds until approval issued.
hazards: Work proceeds without consultant approval — incorrect repair method or depth applied
Consultant inspection delayed — schedule impact and work package standing idle
Inadequate documentation of approval — dispute over approved scope or repair limits
tasks.dominant_hazard: Unapproved structural repair method — potential failure and reinstatement cost
controls: Obtain written scope of works from structural or façade consultant naming the building section, defect type, repair method (stitching depth, spalling depth, coating product), and acceptance criteria before site inspection.
Schedule consultant inspection with 5 working days notice. Confirm site access, scaffold availability, and weather window with PM before inspection date.
Brief consultant on actual scaffold configuration, access method, and any site changes since initial scope. Provide as-built scaffold drawings and load documentation.
Accompany consultant during inspection. Record crack locations, spalling extent, and coating substrate condition using photographs and marked drawings. Document any scope variation identified.

Obtain consultant sign-off on inspection report naming approved repair locations, stitching depths (mm), spalling removal depths (mm), coating type and surface preparation method, and hold points for each repair zone.

If inspection reveals scope change (additional cracking, deeper spalling, substrate contamination, or coating incompatibility), confirm revised scope, method, and timeline with consultant and PM before proceeding.
File signed approval with project QA records. Issue copy to site supervisor and trade contractor. Do not start repair work until approval is issued and held on site.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start crack stitching or spalling repair until: Consultant inspection is complete and written approval of repair locations, depths, method, and coating strategy is signed and held on site.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: Consultant inspection cannot be completed within agreed timeframe due to access, weather, or site condition.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Inspection reveals defects or substrate condition outside the original approved scope.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Approval documentation is incomplete, unsigned, or does not name specific repair locations and depths.

Scaffolding Licence — class confirmed suitable for scaffold height and load. Copy held on site.

Insurance — confirm structural consultant is engaged under professional indemnity cover and scope is documented in writing.

Dust mask (P2) if dry grinding is anticipated during inspection observation

monitoring.frequency: Before any scaffold-based repair work commences
monitoring.evidence: Signed consultant inspection report and approval letter held in project QA file with date, locations marked on as-built drawings, and repair depths (mm) stated.

tasks.task: Crack stitching and concrete spalling repair
tasks.scope: Install stainless-steel crack stitches in mapped cracks per engineer approval. Repair spalling with concrete patching compound or resin injection. Level and fair all repairs flush with surrounding facade. Cure as per product specification.
hazards: Fall from height — worker on platform drilling anchor holes or installing stitches at height >4m
Chemical inhalation — epoxy resin vapours during spalling repair application and curing
Dust inhalation during drilling for crack stitches
Inadequate resin pot life management — defective repair if cure time exceeded
Sharp or protruding stitch anchors — laceration hazard during installation or curing phase
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from working platform >4m during anchor drilling or stitch installation
controls: Use engineered working platform, guardrails, and fall arrest system for work >4m
Provide MSDS for epoxy resin and spalling repair products on site before work starts
Fit dust collection or local exhaust ventilation to drilling equipment
Pre-plan resin application: prepare pot, apply, and cure in one shift per product spec
Install temporary edge protection around completed repairs until cured
Supervisor to verify platform safety and PPE before work starts
Daily weather check: do not apply epoxy in rain, high humidity, or temperatures outside product range
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — Engineer approval of crack stitch locations and repair method must be on site before drilling starts
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: fall protection system not in place or certified before worker reaches platform
🛑 STOP WORK if: MSDS not available or worker has not received product induction
🛑 STOP WORK if: resin pot life exceeded or environmental conditions outside product specification
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain engineer approval for crack stitch locations and repair method
Collect MSDS for all epoxy and concrete products
Book working platform and fall arrest equipment
Plan resin application timing to suit cure schedule
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Dust mask or respirator (if drilling produces visible dust)

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: before work starts and each shift
monitoring.evidence: Visual check of harness fit, anchor point load test, platform edge protection

responsibility.SUP: Verify engineer approval, platform safety, PPE fit, MSDS availability, and sign off hold point
responsibility.WKR: Wear fall arrest system, follow product instructions, report hazards, comply with all controls

tasks.task: Erect modular scaffold to all four elevations with edge protection
tasks.scope: Install working platform to 4.5m minimum height, guardrails, toe boards, working platforms at all levels, exclusion netting below scaffold, safe access (stairs or ramps), certified erector, inspection before occupation.
hazards: Fall from height — incomplete guardrail or toe board installation
Scaffold instability — inadequate base support, uneven ground, or insufficient bracing
Fall of tools or scaffold components during erection — struck-by hazard to ground-level personnel or occupants
Inadequate inspection before occupation — defective platform or guardrail undetected
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from working platform >4m — unsuitable erection or missing edge protection
controls: Confirm ground is level and bearing capacity adequate for scaffold base load — level any high spots or lay base plates on stable soil before erection starts.
Erect scaffold according to manufacturer manual and licensed scaffolder's approved method — no deviations without written engineer approval.
Install guardrails (min 950mm height, mid-rail, toe board) to all four elevations before any worker accesses platform — check for loose fixings or gaps.
Secure exclusion netting below scaffold from base to minimum 1m height to catch falling tools, clips, or components — check netting is tear-free before occupation.
Install safe access (stairs or approved ramp) with handrails to all working levels — do not allow climbing ladders or cross-bracing as primary access.
Tag scaffold platform only after licensed scaffolder completes erection and project supervisor signs inspection certificate — no occupation without tag.
Barricade ground perimeter below scaffold — restrict access to unauthorised personnel or building occupants during erection.
tell building occupants of scaffold erection schedule and fall risk — post warning signs at entry points.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not occupy any working platform until: licensed scaffolder certifies erection is complete and project supervisor signs platform inspection certificate confirming guardrails, toe boards, bracing, and access stairs are installed and secure.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed to erection until: ground bearing capacity is confirmed adequate and base plates are level and stable.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: guardrail, mid-rail, or toe board is missing, loose, or damaged at any level.
🛑 STOP WORK if: exclusion netting is torn, incomplete, or not installed below scaffold.
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold base settles, shifts, or shows signs of instability or uneven bearing.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

Obtain signed handover certificate from licensed scaffolder before any worker occupies platform.
Confirm all personnel accessing scaffold hold current White Card (CPCCWHS1001) and working at heights competency (RIIOHS204E or equivalent).
Verify scaffolder holds valid scaffolding licence appropriate to scaffold type and height.
Post warning signs and tell building occupants of fall risk and exclusion zone.
Record scaffold inspection certificate and handover certificate on site file.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Fall arrest harness and lanyard when working at edges during erection (before guardrails are complete)

monitoring.critical_control: Verify guardrails, mid-rails, toe boards, and safe access stairs installed and secure at all levels before platform occupation.
monitoring.frequency: Before each working level is released for occupation; daily visual check during use
monitoring.evidence: Signed platform inspection certificate; photographic record of guardrails and access points; handover certificate

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold or EWP certification, supervise erection, sign off load checks
responsibility.WKR: Follow erection plan, wear harness at height, report defects

tasks.task: Apply primer and anti-carbonation coating system
tasks.scope: Prime all repaired and exposed concrete surfaces with nominated primer. Apply two-coat anti-carbonation coating system per product data sheet. Allow cure between coats. Protect applied areas from rain and occupant contact.
hazards: Fall from height — painter on working platform applying coating at >4m with wet surfaces creating slip hazard
Solvent inhalation — VOC vapours from primer or coating product during application
Inadequate ventilation on occupied building — fume migration into tenancies
Coating failure if applied in rain or high humidity — incomplete cure or adhesion loss
Slippery working platforms after coating application — increased slip and fall risk
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from working platform >4m — wet coating creates slip hazard
controls: Obtain SDS for primer and coating on site before application starts. Review Section 8 (exposure controls) and Section 11 (toxicology) with applicator and supervisor.
Install continuous mechanical ventilation — extract fumes from work zone directly away from building interior. Maintain positive outward air flow across platform during and 2 hours after application.
Barricade platform edges and wet coated surfaces with high-visibility tape and warning signs. No workers to enter until surfaces are touch-dry and slip hazard ceases.
Verify weather forecast — do not start if rain forecast within 24 hours. Stop work immediately if rain begins during application or cure window.
Check cure time per product data sheet between coats. Do not apply second coat until first coat has reached specified hard-dry or tack-free state.
Confirm scaffold is clean, dry, and free of trip hazards before painter moves to platform. Remove wet coating drips daily to prevent slip hazard accumulation.
Verify all occupant windows and doors in spray zone are closed. Brief building occupants of application schedule and ventilation requirements before work starts.
Wear organic vapour respirator (half-mask, cartridge rated to product VOC per SDS Section 8). Do not use P2 dust mask — solvent vapours need vapour cartridge.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply primer until: SDS reviewed, ventilation system tested and running, and weather forecast confirms no rain within 24-hour cure window
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply second coat until: first coat hard-dry time per product data sheet confirmed by site supervisor and documented on log
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: rain begins during application or forecasted within cure window cannot be met
🛑 STOP WORK if: mechanical ventilation fails or cannot maintain outward air flow — do not resume until extract system tested and confirmed working
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant fume complaints received — cease application, increase ventilation, and obtain site supervisor approval to resume
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Scaffold erection permit signed by licenced scaffolder and handover certificate obtained before painter accesses platform.
Working at heights permit completed and signed before each application session.
Site supervisor to conduct daily weather check before work start and at end of each shift.
Log first and second coat application dates, cure times, and weather conditions on site documentation.
Brief all building occupants on application dates, times, and ventilation strategy. Provide contact number for fume complaints.
Supervisor to monitor occupant feedback during and 48 hours after coating application completion.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Organic vapour respirator (half-mask with solvent cartridge rated to product VOC)
Hard hat (when working on open scaffold platform)

monitoring.critical_control: Verify mechanical extract ventilation running continuously and positive outward air flow confirmed at platform edge before and during application.
monitoring.frequency: Before each application start, every 2 hours during application, and continuously for 2 hours after application ceases
monitoring.evidence: Supervisor sign-off on site log confirming ventilation status and weather window check. Occupant feedback log (no complaints recorded). Cure time log documenting hard-dry verification before second coat application.

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold and fall arrest systems, enforce exclusion zone, check SDS
responsibility.WKR: Use harness and lanyard, wear respiratory protection, report faults

tasks.task: Apply textured acrylic render finish coat to all elevations
tasks.scope: Apply two-coat textured acrylic render finish to all facade panels. Blend edges at scaffold cuts and repair margins. Match existing facade texture and colour profile. Allow full cure. Protect applied finishes during curing.
hazards: Fall from height — render application on working platform >4m, especially near scaffold edges during blending
Slippery platform surface from wet render spray — increased slip and fall risk
Inadequate weather protection — rain or high wind during application causes defective finish requiring rework
Render overspray into occupied areas — cosmetic damage to windows, doors, or occupant property
Repetitive strain injury — prolonged spray or roller application
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from working platform >4m during render application and blending
controls: Confirm scaffold handover certificate signed and on-site before any worker accesses platform.
Verify working at heights permit issued and current for this task before starting.
Check edge protection (guardrail or equivalent 1.1m height) installed on all scaffold platform edges before work starts.
Lay non-slip matting or grip tape on platform surfaces where render will be applied or sprayed.
Apply render only when wind speed is below 15 km/h; stop work if wind exceeds limit.
Establish wet-render work zone on platform — restrict movement outside blending perimeter; use rope delineation.
Wear full-body harness and lanyard anchored to independent fixed point during blending at scaffold edges; check harness before each use.
Operate spray equipment with two-handed control; do not apply finish during rain or wet weather.

critical_controls.occupied_interface: All tenancy exclusion, access, and drop-zone protection must be established before any scaffold erection or facade work begins and maintained throughout works. No exceptions.

task_blocks_raw.task: Dismantle scaffold, remove exclusion barriers, and reinstate occupant access
task_blocks_raw.scope: Dismantle all scaffold in reverse erection order. Remove guardrails, platforms, and edge protection. Clear all exclusion barriers and signage. Reinstate normal building access to all floors. Sweep and clean facade base.
hazards: Fall from height — dismantler on platform >4m removing guardrails and edge protection
Falling scaffold components or guardrails striking workers below or occupants
Occupants re-entering work zone before clearance is complete — struck by falling debris
Incomplete removal of exclusion barriers or netting — trip hazard or visual obstruction remaining
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from platform >4m during scaffold dismantling after removal of guardrails
controls: Dismantle scaffold in reverse erection order — remove internal bracing and props before removing standards and ledgers.
Establish exclusion zone around scaffold base — extend 2 m beyond footprint — barricade with tape and warning signs before dismantling commences.
Appoint spotter on ground — dedicated role, positioned to follow falling debris and warn workers or approaching occupants.
Lower all scaffold components vertically using rope or controlled lowering system — do not drop or throw components.
Remove guardrails last — only after all platform planks and cross-bracing are removed — no platform standing after guardrail removal.
Use harness and lanyard attached to independent anchor point — dismantler must remain belayed throughout dismantling.
Check each connection before removal — confirm bolts are free and connections are not corroded or stuck before loosening.
Remove exclusion netting and barriers systematically — do not leave partial netting or signage that may obstruct sightlines or create trip hazards.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not dismantle first standard or ledger until: licenced scaffolder has verified reverse erection sequence and all dismantling team understand the load path.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not reinstate occupant access until: exclusion zone is fully cleared, all barriers and netting removed, debris swept, and project manager has signed off completion.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: guardrails are removed before internal bracing is released — workers will be unprotected on platform.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupants attempt to enter work zone while scaffold dismantling is in progress — re-establish exclusion zone and brief occupants on restricted access.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any scaffold component shows unexpected damage, corrosion, or loose connection during dismantling — consult licenced scaffolder before proceeding.
